This extraction +The direct `common-name` supplies the canonical label whenever that slot exists; +an empty, duplicate or malformed direct name fails instead of triggering another +name search. When the slot is entirely absent, a bounded native enzyme-name +rule supports a `Protein-Complexes` member with one component at integer +coefficient two or greater and exactly one resolved `catalyzes/Enzymatic-Reaction`. +That activity must have a coherent META identity, exactly one enzyme reference +back to the same complex, one coherent native reaction reference and one string +`common-name`. The resulting authority retains the exact complex ID. SRI's +[BioCyc loader manual](https://bioinformatics.ai.sri.com/biowarehouse/repos/biocyc-loader/flatfile/doc/biocyc-manual.html) +documents linked activity names for proteins lacking `COMMON-NAME`, and its +[`full-enzyme-name` function](https://bioinformatics.ai.sri.com/ptools/ptools-fns.html) +describes native protein naming from those slots. The adapter implements only +the single-activity homomer case; unnamed monomers, heteromers, absent or +noninteger coefficients, multiple activities (even with identical names), and +unresolved or mismatched back-references remain unsupported. It does not +concatenate activity names or add assembly words to a label. + +Both name paths decode native inline presentation markup and character entities, +with no curated-label fallback or imported synonyms, including activity aliases. +Malformed or still-escaped numeric references and decoded characters outside the +supported XML character ranges are rejected; references are not recursively +unescaped to guess a label. Component, organism and curator names are not +emitted as authority terms. Apart from the explicitly validated enzyme-name +relation, nested names are not used. Nested unresolved protein references do +not imply unresolved identity of a directly named full top-level object. This extraction establishes identifier/name provenance, not species/strain equivalence, assembly, sequence, reaction or experimental function.
